_comment: What the night queue actually did with each mawshift Issue, from the run of
2026-09-22. Ground truth is whether the Issue produced usable work, read from
the repository's pull requests and the incident report's reclassification.
openclaw reported '0 succeeded, 17 failed', every one of them
worker_output_invalid. That was false for all 17. Its night runner parses the
old CLI envelope shape (result.text) while OpenClaw 2026.9.5 returns
payloads[].text and final, so every worker's valid final JSON read as
undefined. Filed as openclaw-config #27. Scoring against that report would
have taught the gate to predict a schema mismatch.
The gate was not installed on mawshift when this run happened. These outcomes
were recorded first; the evaluations beside them were collected afterwards,
in dry-run, without writing to any Issue. The gate reads Issue text and never
sees the runner, so collecting its answers after the fact does not leak the
result into the prediction.
'cause' names why a failure happened, because only some failures are knowable
from an Issue. A dependency on unmerged code is visible in the Issue text. A
worker emitting NO_REPLY instead of its final JSON is not.
Design Issues count as succeeded when they produced the decision they asked
for and unblocked their successors. They open no pull request, which openclaw
separately miscounts as missing_pr; that is the runner's completion model, not
the Issue failing.
run: night_issue 2026-09-22, sige31ymail/mawshift, 17 Issues, 15 produced usable work

23.evidence: design Issue: settled the side-scroller pause/resume specification and unblocked #32 and #33. No PR by design

24.evidence: design Issue: settled the HUD overlap approach and unblocked #34. No PR by design

27.evidence: the worker's final assistant text was NO_REPLY rather than the required JSON, so nothing was produced. A property of the worker, not of the Issue

28.evidence: the gate could not judge it: this evaluation ran after the run had closed the Issue, so the gate failed closed on a closed Issue. During the night run itself #28 was open and produced its design decision (unblocking #36). Not scorable either way

30.evidence: the worker stopped deliberately: #17 and #18 were still open, their PRs #38 and #39 unmerged, and the fog and procedural-texture work they carry was absent from its worktree. The Issue body states the dependency outright

33.evidence: PR #45. Stacked on #32's branch, so the verify workflow's main-targeting condition did not run it; the pull request was produced

35.evidence: PR #47, verify success. Contested: the Issue body declares 'BLOCKED: do not queue until #27's spec is transcribed', and #27 produced nothing (NO_REPLY), so its own unblock condition was never met. A PR exists, but the gate's block was defensible
